description: Agent-based, network-embedded simulation of mask adoption under social influence, policy, media exposure, and supply constraints, optionally coupled with SEIR disease dynamics. Individuals interact via a small-world social network and co-locate in daily schedules (household, work/school, retail, public transport). Adoption is driven by a probabilistic choice model integrating social, policy, media, risk, habit, and availability signals. Retail market dynamics determine mask availability and price. A stochastic SEIR process models infection transmission modified by mask efficacy and location factors.

parameters.vaccination_status: Bernoulli(0.6) independent of age by default
parameters.location_schedule: Home nightly; Work for workforce_fraction on weekdays; School for school_age_fraction; Retail visits Poisson(retail_visit_rate_per_week/7); Public transport Bernoulli(public_transport_use_fraction) on commute days
parameters.network_neighbors: Watts-Strogatz small-world with average_degree and rewiring
parameters.past_infection_experience: 0 initially for most; seed with initial infections

parameters.counts: derived from population and attendance rates; retail ~ retailer_count; workplaces ~ ceil(population_size*workforce_fraction/30); schools ~ ceil(population_size*school_age_fraction/200); public_transport ~ max(10, ceil(population_size*public_transport_use_fraction/300))
parameters.capacity: type-specific: households=household size; workplace~30; school~200; retail~50; public_transport~40 scaled by location_capacity_multiplier
parameters.operating_hours: workplace/school weekdays; retail daily; public_transport daily extended

modules.name: MaskAdoptionDecision
modules.description: Computes daily mask-wearing decisions for each individual based on social, policy, media, risk, habit, and availability signals; updates habit and inventory consumption.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each Individual i:
  loc <- current location from i.location_schedule
  policy_req <- signals.policy.mask_requirement_by_location[loc.id]
  enforce_p <- signals.policy.enforcement_probability_by_location[loc.id]
  social_rate <- mean(mask_adoption_state among i.network_neighbors) if neighbors exist else 0
  household_rate <- mean(mask_adoption_state among household members excluding i)
  social_signal <- social_influence_weight * (i.social_influence_susceptibility * social_rate) + household_norm_weight * household_rate
  media_signal <- media_effect_weight * (signals.media.risk_message_index * i.trust_in_authorities)
  risk_signal <- i.risk_perception
  policy_signal <- policy_req * (enforce_p * i.compliance_propensity)
  availability <- 1 if i.mask_inventory > 0 else 0
  utility <- social_signal + media_signal + risk_signal + policy_signal - mask_discomfort_cost
  p_wear <- availability * sigmoid(logistic_slope_beta * (utility - peer_threshold))
  new_state <- Bernoulli(p_wear)
  if new_state == 1: i.mask_inventory <- max(0, i.mask_inventory - 1)
  # habit update
  if new_state == 1: i.habit_strength <- min(habit_max, i.habit_strength + habit_formation_rate*(1 - i.habit_strength))
  else: i.habit_strength <- max(0, i.habit_strength * (1 - habit_decay_rate))
  # risk perception small update from habit and past infection experience
  i.risk_perception <- clip( i.risk_perception + 0.02*i.past_infection_experience + 0.01*(household_rate - 0.5), 0, 1 )
notes: peer_threshold is the internal adoption threshold; when utility exceeds it, probability approaches 1
Availability gates wearing; separate purchase decision handled in market module

requirements: Neighbor and household masks for social_rate

modules.name: PolicyComplianceAndEnforcement
modules.description: Sets policy level over time, translates mandates to location mask requirements and enforcement probabilities, and issues fines for noncompliance at entry checks.

update_rule.pseudocode:
policy_level <- initial_policy_level if day < policy_start_day else update_by_thresholds(Re_daily, mandate_Re_threshold)
for each Location L:
  if policy_level == 'none': req<-0; enforce_p<-0
  if policy_level == 'recommendation': req<-0; enforce_p<-0
  if policy_level == 'mandate': req<-1; enforce_p<- enforcement_strength * enforcement_check_probability_base * L.baseline_contact_rate
  signals.policy.mask_requirement_by_location[L.id] <- req
  signals.policy.enforcement_probability_by_location[L.id] <- clip(enforce_p, 0, 1)
# Entry checks and fines
fines_today <- 0; noncomp_count <- 0; mandate_visits <- 0
for each Individual i at entry events to locations with req==1:
  mandate_visits += 1
  if i.mask_adoption_state == 0:
    noncomp_count += 1
    if Bernoulli(signals.policy.enforcement_probability_by_location[loc.id] * ticket_probability_base):
      fines_today += fine_amount
observables.policy.fines_daily <- fines_today
if mandate_visits > 0: observables.policy.noncompliance_rate_under_mandate <- noncomp_count / mandate_visits else 0
notes: update_by_thresholds raises level to mandate if Re exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive days; can also relax if Re below 0.9 for 7 days
Enforcement probability scales with enforcement_strength and location contact intensity

requirements: Entry event approximations based on attendance

modules.name: MediaExposureAndBeliefs
modules.description: Generates daily public health messages and media broadcasts; updates individual risk perception and trust according to exposure, outlet bias, and misinformation.

update_rule.pseudocode:
if day % max(1, round(1/communication_frequency)) == 0:
  pha_msg <- baseline risk-reducing message intensity = 1.0
else:
  pha_msg <- 0.5
# Aggregate media signals
risk_index <- 0
for each MediaOutlet m:
  content <- pha_msg * (1 - m.misinformation_rate) + m.message_bias
  risk_index += content * m.reach * m.credibility
signals.media.risk_message_index <- clip(risk_index, -1, 2)
# Update individual beliefs
for each Individual i:
  exposure <- weighted sum of outlets in i.media_exposure_profile by reach
  delta_risk <- media_belief_gain * exposure * signals.media.risk_message_index
  i.risk_perception <- clip( (1 - media_effect_decay)*i.risk_perception + delta_risk, 0, 1 )
  # trust nudged towards outlet credibility weighted by PHA consistency
  i.trust_in_authorities <- clip( i.trust_in_authorities + 0.01*exposure*(mean_credibility - 0.6), 0, 1 )
notes: media_belief_gain is derived from media_effect_weight implicitly via MaskAdoptionDecision; here we use fixed gain 0.05 internally
media_effect_decay controls memory of prior perceptions

requirements: Media outlets list with reach and credibility

modules.name: DiseaseTransmissionAndProgression
modules.description: Simulates stochastic SEIR progression and transmission via contacts at locations; computes daily Re.

update_rule.pseudocode:
new_infections <- 0
contacts_considered <- 0
for each Location L:
  attendees <- individuals scheduled at L today
  # Sample pair contacts using binomial approximation of random mixing
  for each susceptible s in attendees where s.health_state == 'S':
    lambda <- 0
    for each infectious j in attendees where j.health_state == 'I':
      p_base <- base_transmission_rate * contact_rate_mod[L.type] * (1/ L.ventilation_factor)
      eff_out <- mask_outward_efficacy * quality_multiplier(j.mask_quality) if j.mask_adoption_state==1 else 0
      eff_in <- mask_inward_efficacy * quality_multiplier(s.mask_quality) if s.mask_adoption_state==1 else 0
      p_eff <- p_base * (1 - eff_out) * (1 - eff_in)
      lambda += p_eff
      contacts_considered += 1
    if Bernoulli(1 - exp(-lambda)) == 1:
      s.health_state <- 'E'; s.past_infection_experience <- min(1, s.past_infection_experience + 0.5)
      new_infections += 1
# Progression E->I and I->R
for each Individual i:
  if i.health_state == 'E' and Bernoulli(1/incubation_period_mean) == 1: i.health_state <- 'I'
  if i.health_state == 'I' and Bernoulli(1/infectious_period_mean) == 1: i.health_state <- 'R'
# Compute prevalence and Re
I_t <- count of health_state=='I'
observables.epi.infections_daily <- new_infections
observables.epi.prevalence_daily <- I_t / population_size
Re_daily <- (new_infections + epsilon) / (I_t + epsilon) * infectious_period_mean
observables.epi.Re_daily <- Re_daily
notes: Lambda approximation emulates cumulative risk from infectious attendees
epsilon is a small number 1e-6 to avoid division by zero

requirements: Attendance lists per location per day

modules.name: MaskMarketAndRetail
modules.description: Handles mask purchases, retailer stock flows, price adjustments, and inventory allocation.

update_rule.pseudocode:
# Restock pipeline
for each Retailer r:
  incoming <- Poisson(r.restock_rate * r.backlog) after supply_lead_time_days delay
  r.stock_level += incoming
# Price update by demand pressure
for each Retailer r:
  demand_pressure <- r.yesterday_demand / max(1, r.yesterday_supply)
  price_multiplier <- 1 + price_adjustment_sensitivity * (demand_pressure - 1)
  r.price[cloth] <- max(0.5, mask_price_cloth * price_multiplier)
  r.price[surgical] <- max(0.75, mask_price_surgical * price_multiplier)
  r.price[respirator] <- max(1.0, mask_price_respirator * price_multiplier)
# Individual purchase decisions
for each Individual i:
  if i.mask_inventory <= purchase_reorder_point and Bernoulli(purchase_intent_prob) == 1:
    # choose retailer uniformly nearby (no explicit space) and pick quality by quality_mix and income
    budget <- min(0.01 * i.income, 20)
    target_qty <- purchase_target_inventory - i.mask_inventory
    buy_quality <- argmax over types of (quality_multiplier * (i.income / price))
    purchasable <- min(target_qty, floor(budget / r.price[buy_quality]), r.stock_level[buy_quality])
    r.stock_level[buy_quality] -= purchasable
    i.mask_inventory += purchasable
# Observables
observables.market.stockout_daily <- fraction of retailers with any type stock_level == 0
observables.market.avg_price_daily <- average over retailers and types weighted by daily sales
notes: purchase_intent_prob defaults to 0.6 for those intending to wear; can be derived from habit_strength
Simple restock pipeline can be implemented with queues of delayed orders

modules.name: AdoptionAndEpiAggregator
modules.description: Aggregates daily adoption and epidemiological statistics by location and overall; computes stockout frequency and policy cost accumulation.

update_rule.pseudocode:
adoption_rate <- mean(i.mask_adoption_state for all individuals)
by_loc <- for each location type T: mean(masking among attendees in T today)
cum_infections <- cumulative sum of observables.epi.infections_daily
peak_prev <- max historical observables.epi.prevalence_daily
Re_series <- observables.epi.Re_daily
noncomp <- rolling value from observables.policy.noncompliance_rate_under_mandate
stockout_freq <- cumulative days with stockout / day
avg_price <- moving average of observables.market.avg_price_daily weighted by sales
policy_costs <- cumulative sum of observables.policy.fines_daily
emit all as observables
notes: Aggregation should be consistent with attendance sampling
stockout_frequency is fraction up to current day

requirements: Access to historical time series buffers

algorithms.AdoptionDecisionLogit: Probabilistic choice using sigmoid on weighted utility of social, policy, media, risk, habit, and discomfort components gated by availability.
algorithms.SEIR_Stochastic: Discrete-time SEIR with Bernoulli transitions and contact-based exposure using location-modified transmission probabilities.
algorithms.WattsStrogatzNetwork: Small-world social network generator with given average degree and rewiring probability.
algorithms.PriceAdjustmentByDemand: Retail price updates proportionally to demand/supply ratio with sensitivity parameter; simple restock pipeline with lead time.
algorithms.Re_Estimation: Daily ratio of new infections to current infectious times mean infectious period with smoothing epsilon.
